long_biography.plain_text:
Basketball has supplied the most durable thread in Bill Laurie's public life. The Versailles, Missouri, guard played for Memphis State in the 1973 NCAA championship game before becoming a teacher and high-school coach. He was inducted into the Missouri Sports Hall of Fame in 2003 for contributions as a player, coach, executive and benefactor.

Laurie converted that sporting interest into professional ownership when he and Nancy Walton Laurie acquired the St. Louis Blues and their arena. They eventually sold both. Their support for the University of Memphis helped finance an athletics-facilities programme and the Laurie-Walton Family Basketball Center, returning his involvement to the institution where he had played.
